## Introduction

Real mediation studies rarely have complete data, and the underlying variables
are rarely normal. **medsim** ships a set of reusable data-generating utilities
and estimator adapters — added for the *Missing Effect* study (MBCO-MI vs.
Monte-Carlo CI under missingness x nonnormality) — for simulating mediation
analysis under `MCAR`/`MAR`/`MNAR` missingness and Fleishman-power
nonnormality.

This vignette walks through generating nonnormal data, amputating it under a
missingness mechanism, and comparing two ways to test the indirect effect under
multiple imputation: the D4-stacked MBCO likelihood-ratio test (`MBCO-MI`) and
the Monte-Carlo product interval on the Rubin-pooled paths (`MC-CI`).

## Installation

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false
pak::pak("Data-Wise/medsim")
```

`medsim_method_mbco_mi()` needs `mice` (multiple imputation); without it, it
degrades to a complete-case MBCO chi-square test. Install the full stack for
the validated D4-stacked pooling:

```{r}
#| label: install-suggests
#| eval: false
install.packages(c("mice", "mitml", "RMediation"))
```

## Step 1: Generate Nonnormal Data

`medsim_rnonnormal()` draws values with a target skew/kurtosis using the
Fleishman power method:

```{r}
#| label: rnonnormal
library(medsim)

x <- medsim_rnonnormal(n = 500, mean = 0, sd = 1, skew = 1.5, kurtosis = 5)
c(mean = mean(x), sd = sd(x))
```

## Step 2: Insert Missingness

`medsim_amputate()` inserts `NA`s into the `target` column(s) under a chosen
missingness mechanism (MCAR, MAR, or MNAR), with a logistic amputer calibrated
to the target proportion `prop`:

```{r}
#| label: amputate
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(X = rnorm(500), M = rnorm(500), Y = rnorm(500))

d_mar <- medsim_amputate(d, target = "M", mechanism = "MAR", prop = 0.3)
mean(is.na(d_mar$M))
```

## Step 3: Define a Missing-Data Scenario

`medsim_scenario_missing()` builds a single scenario combining the generating
paths (`true_params`: `a`, `b`, `cp`), an amputation mechanism, a target missing
proportion, and optional nonnormal residuals. `medsim_scenario_missing_grid()`
crosses a list of effect-size cells with mechanisms, proportions, and residual
shapes, the building block for a full missing-data simulation study:

```{r}
#| label: scenario
scn <- medsim_scenario_missing(
  name = "MAR-30pct",
  true_params = list(a = 0.39, b = 0.39, cp = 0.14),
  mechanism = "MAR",
  prop = 0.3
)

grid <- medsim_scenario_missing_grid(
  true_params_list = list(
    small  = list(a = 0.14, b = 0.14, cp = 0.14),
    medium = list(a = 0.39, b = 0.39, cp = 0.14)
  ),
  mechanisms = c("MCAR", "MAR", "MNAR"),
  props = c(0.1, 0.3),
  nonnormal_list = list(normal = NULL, skew = list(skew = 1.5, kurtosis = 4))
)
length(grid)
```

## Step 4: Run Both Estimators

`medsim_method_mbco_mi()` and `medsim_method_mc_ci()` are factories: each
returns a function with the `method(data, params)` contract and the same 6-field
core result. `medsim_run()` takes one method, so run each and compare the
results scenario by scenario. (MBCO-MI additionally emits branch diagnostics:
`indirect_p_fixed`, `branch_mix`, `p_branch_a`, `stacked_branch`, `r4`,
`r4_fixed`.)

```{r}
#| label: run
results <- medsim_run(
  method = medsim_method_mbco_mi(model = NULL, m = 20),
  scenarios = list(scn),
  config = medsim_config("test")
)
results_mc <- medsim_run(
  method = medsim_method_mc_ci(model = NULL, m = 20),
  scenarios = list(scn),
  config = medsim_config("test")
)

summary(results)
```

### Fixed-branch correction and the reference degrees of freedom

Two options of `medsim_method_mbco_mi()` change how the D4 test is referred to
its `F` distribution. Neither changes the data, the imputations, or the D4
statistic:

- `ariv = "fixed"` computes the relative increase in variance (`r4`) from
  per-imputation statistics on the branch that the stacked constrained fit
  selects, so imputations that disagree on the branch cannot deflate it. This is the
  default; `ariv = "own"` is the standard Chan-Meng pooling and can be
  liberal at high missingness. Both p-values are
  always returned (`indirect_p`, `indirect_p_fixed`); `ariv` chooses which one
  fills `indirect_p`.
- `df = "chan_meng"` uses the Chan and Meng (2022, eq. 2.15) denominator degrees
  of freedom, as `mitml::testModels(method = "D4")` does. This is the
  default; `df = "li"` keeps the Li et al. (1991) approximation. Only the p-values change.

```{r}
#| label: ariv-df
results_legacy <- medsim_run(
  method = medsim_method_mbco_mi(model = NULL, m = 20, ariv = "own", df = "li"),
  scenarios = list(scn),
  config = medsim_config("test")
)
```

## Step 5: Branch-Switch Diagnostics

MBCO fits the union null `ab = 0` as the better of two single-path fits,
`a = 0` or `b = 0`, and the imputations of one dataset can disagree on which
branch wins. Each MBCO-MI row records the majority branch (`branch_switch`,
1 = `a = 0`) and whether the imputations disagreed (`branch_mix`).
`medsim_summarize_branch_switch()` reports, per scenario, the share of
replicates in which the `a = 0` branch wins:

```{r}
#| label: branch-switch
medsim_summarize_branch_switch(results)
```

## Optional: Inverse-Probability Weighting

A thin IPW adapter, `medsim_method_ipw()`, is also available for comparison
against the imputation-based approaches:

```{r}
#| label: ipw
results_ipw <- medsim_run(
  method = medsim_method_ipw(model = NULL),
  scenarios = list(scn),
  config = medsim_config("test")
)
```

## Next Steps

- See `vignette("getting-started")` for the general `medsim_run()` workflow.
- See `vignette("estimand-kinds")` for how missing-data scenarios relate to
  the estimand-kind system used elsewhere in medsim.
- `medsim_method_mbco_mi()` reproduces the `mitml::testModels(method = "D4")`
  statistic when `mice`/`mitml` are installed (Reiter/Chan-Meng D4 pooling). Its
  p-value matches `mitml` (with `ariv = "positive"`) under the default `df = "chan_meng"`;
  `df = "li"` gives the legacy Li et al. (1991) denominator df.
